The project had a major inactivity period even though its overall activity was relatively steady outside of that gap. The longest gap was somewhat difficult to interpret because the commits immediately before it mainly involved normal compatibility, CI, documentation, and maintenance work rather than an obvious event that caused development to stop.

Based on the surrounding commits, I think the gap was most likely a pause between maintenance or release cycles rather than complete abandonment. Activity eventually returned through dependency and compatibility updates, a version bump, and build-related work. This suggests the project did recover, although the type of work after the gap was focused more on maintenance than major new development.

## Project Statistics

- Activity Pattern: cyclical
- Longest Gap: 2023-02 to 2025-06
- Longest Gap Length: 29 months
- Number of Gaps of at Least 3 Months: 3
- Has Recovered: Yes
